column9: The recommendation states that there should be a validation check after the user input. This would allow invalid input and then throw an error. It might be better to not allow certain inputs by visually marking the days available for selection and making invalid dates non-selectable.
column16: There is an asterisk next to the event title field to indicate that it is mandatory. All the other fields do not have an asterisk and therefore it seems not necessary to print errors in the video case. The recommendation could include an "advanced settings" tab where all the optional information fields could be hidden to not confuse the user.

column9: I think that at least the system checks after pressing a store button.

There are numerous input fields, ... on this page. If there is a usability issue with one of them it should state which field and where to find it - if there is an issue with an entire category it should mention that (e.g. "All input fields with datepicker"). Plus, why should there be an error message? The standard practice would be to disable the days that are before the start date and maybe even preselect the next day automatically ...
column16: If there is only one required field (name) as indicated by the * next to the title of the field, this is not really apparent/relevant based on the video. But YES, if there were more required fields, it would be important to clearly mark these fields first before thinking about error prevention. Anyone who has "detected" this issue based on the video is able to read minds.
column23: There is always the possibility to click on the logo or "Events" button in the navigation to go back. However, a "Cancel" or back button would be sufficient - definitely not on the bottom of the page though. If I open the page and want to go back, a user is not thinking about scrolling down to the bottom of the page to find this button.
column29: It could be EXTREMELY useful if the suggestions would actually be of better quality, find real usability problems and also help solve them directly - especially during the design process. However, since this is a video of a online version or at least a programmed prototype - this is not really part of the design process. Usually the planning, design, testing, ... (iterative user-centered design process) is done with Figma, ... and Interactive Clickdummies/Prototypes/...
